name: Coarse strainer
description: Easily separate and remove large matter carried along by the raw water, which might negatively affect the efficiency of later treatment procedures or make their implementation more difficult. Mesh opening larger than 4 cm.
advantage: Low maintenance required. Accomodates with high flow rate. Reduced risk of clogging.
disadvantage: Limited removal of small particles. Not suitable for fine screening.  Requires large footprint.

name: Strainer
description: Strainers with mesh opening between 0.5 and 3 cm to remove large matter, e.g. leaves or duckweed. Usually applied for surface water intake.
advantage: Moderate maintenance required. Could be used for different treatment applications. Low risk of equipment damage.
disadvantage: Limited removal of fine particles. Limitations in accomodating high flow rates. Requires a large footprint.

name: Micro strainer
description: Strainer with mesh opening between 10 to 40 micrometer to remove small particles and algae
advantage: Fine filtration. Enhances water quality. Flexible installation. Low risk of damage.
disadvantage: High maintenance required. Limitations in accomodating high flow rates. Large footprint. High capital and maintenance costs.

name: Cascade with coagulant dosing with ferric chloride
description: Cascade tanks function on the gravity-driven principle, where water flows over a series of steps. Additionally an aerator can be used for dosing of ferric chloride.
advantage: Effective removal of suspended particles, turbidity. Flexibility in terms of adjusting coagulant dosages and mixing parameters based on water quality variations. Proper mixing reduces the amount of coagulant needed. Enhances settling rates, facilitating easier separation of flocs.
disadvantage: Cascade mixing typically requires energy-intensive mixing equipment to ensure thorough dispersion of coagulants. The equipment requires regular maintenance to ensure proper functioning.

name: Lamella clarifier, sloped plates
description: Vessel with a series of inclined plates, water is entering at the top and the sludge is discharged at the bottom.

name: Flotation with saturated air
description: Also referred to as Dissolved Air Flotation (DAF). Pressurized air is released at atmospheric pressure in a flotation tank basin, hence forming tiny bubbles which adhere to the suspended matter, causing the suspended matter to float to the surface of the water. There, the suspended matter is removed by a skimming device.
advantage: Efficient Solid-Liquid Separation. Very small footprint. Very flexible and custmized design. High removal efficiency of NOM, algae and heavy metals.
disadvantage: Requires careful monitoring and control of various parameters, including air flow, pressure, and chemical dosing. It requires additional chemical dosing. Increased operational costs and higher energy consumption. Sludge handling of and disposal that may require additional treatment processes to dewater.

name: Granular activated carbon (GAC) filtration
description: Submerged packed bed filtration with activated carbon granules
advantage: High removal efficiencies (up to 99.9%) for many VOCs, including trichloroethylene (TCE) and tetrachloroethylene (PCE).   In most cases, GAC can remove target contaminants to concentrations below 1 µg/l.Regenerative carbon beds allow for easy recovery of the adsorption media.
disadvantage: Media is to be removed and regenerated when GAC capacity is diminished due to saturation with NOM.

name: Powdered activated carbon (PAC) filtration
description: Filtration with powdered activated carbon.
advantage: High adsporption capacity for pesticides and organic material . Effective removal of taste and odor. PAC can be regenerated and reused to minimize operational costs.
disadvantage: Expensive compared to other activated carbon options such as GAC. Proper mixing and dispersion equipment are required to ensure effective contact between PAC particles. Potential generation of airborne dust. Sludge generation that requires treatment and disposal.

name: Anion exchange (AIEX) filtration unit
description: Packed bed filtration with anion exchange resin beads as filter media
advantage: High removal efficiencies (greater than 99 percent) for negatively charged contaminants.   When the capacity of the resin is exhausted, it can be regenerated to restore it to its initial condition.
disadvantage: The spent regenerant brine is a concentrated solution of the removed contaminants and will be high in dissolved solids and excess regenerant ions. Anion exchange treatment also can lower the pH of the treated water and, therefore, may require post-treatment corrosion control. Disposal of the resin may require a  hazardous waste handling permit.

name: Cation exchange (CIEX) filtration unit
description: Packed bed filtration with cation exchange resin beads as filter media
advantage: Cation exchange is a proven technology for water softening and removal of positively charged contaminants. It can achieve high removal efficiencies (greater than 99 percent) for positively charged contaminants. When the capacity of the resin is exhausted, it can be regenerated to restore it to its initial sorption capacity.
disadvantage: The spent regenerant brine is a concentrated solution of the removed contaminants and will have high concentration levels of solutes and regenerant ions (e.g., sodium and chloride ions). This waste stream will require care when discharged and/or further treatment or disposal.

name: Rapid sand filtration, submerged, single medium
description: Packed bed gravity filtration with a supernatant layer on top and a single filter medium (sand)
advantage: Simple to operate. Lower capital costs. Suitable when total suspended solids (TSS) are moderate.
disadvantage: Limited filtration efficiency for fine particles. Requires more frequent backwashing or media replacement. Has reduced flexibility in achieving filtration goals.

name: Rapid sand filtration, submerged, dual media, sand
description: Packed bed gravity filtration with a supernatant layer on top, an upper layer with coarse sand and a bottom layer with fine sand material
advantage: Double media filtration systems use two layers of different media with varying particle sizes, which can enhance filtration efficiency by capturing a wider range of particle sizes. More effective removal of  TSS. Greater filtration flexibility. Less backwashing required.
disadvantage: High capital costs. Higher design, maintenance ans operational complexity. The use of two media layers increases the potential for media clogging or fouling. Backwashing may cause mixing of the layers, negating positive effects.

name: Rapid sand filtration, submerged, dual media, sand and GAC
description: Packed bed gravity filtration with a supernatant layer on top, an upper sand layer and a bottom layer with granular activated carbon

name: Rapid sand filtration, pressurized
description: Packed bed pressurized filtration

name: Limestone filtration
description: Filtration with limestone to increase the water hardness

name: Pellet softening reactor with lime
description: Hard water passes through a vessel where lime, caustic soda or sodium carbonate is added at the bottom of the vessel to initiate crystallisation of calcium carbonate on fine-grained sand or calcium carbonate beads, called pellets.
advantage: Highly effective in reducing the hardness of water. Minimal chemical usage. Low maintenance required. High flexibility in treatment operations.
disadvantage: Significant amount of sludge. Safety precautions are required to minimize the chemical risks. Additional pH adjustment may be required. Operational control required to minimize the precipitation of pellet chemicals in subsequent treatment stages or in the distribution system.

name: Polymeric microfiltration
description: Filtration with membranes that typically removes particles between 0.1 and 10 micron. Ceramic membranes are resistant to extreme operating conditions and (chemical) cleaning agents.

name: Ceramic microfiltration
description: Filtration with membranes that typically removes particles between 0.1 and 10 micron.

name: Chlorine dosing equipment
advantage: Chlorination is a highly effective method for killing a wide range of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, and protozoa. Chlorine residuals prevent potential regrowth. Provides rapid action in killing microorganisms.
disadvantage: Can lead to the formation of disinfection byproducts (DBPs). Can impact taste and odor of the treated water. Safety precautions or hazardous gases are required. Chlorine can react with materials and metals in the distribution system, leading to corrosion of infrastructure.

name: Main stream nanofiltration
advantage: Effective in selective removal of dissolved ions, organic compounds, and other contaminants. Achieves high recovery of water. Reduces the use of chemicals. Compact design with small footprint.
disadvantage: High energy consumption. Higher mainentance costs and high risk of membrane fouling. Limited removal of small solutes. Sensitive to pH variations in the feed water.

name: Baffled ozone contact reactor
description: Baffle containing vessel for ozone induced oxidation
advantage: Effective disinfection against a wide range of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, and protozoa. Oxidizes a variety of contaminants in water, including organic compounds, taste and odor compounds. No odor or taste residuals unlike other disinfection processes and no disinfection by-products (DBPs).  Requires a shorter conctact time for either micropollutant removal or disinfection. Requires a smaller footprint than other disinfection options.
disadvantage: Expensive to implement and operate due to the high cost of ozone generation equipment, energy requirements, and maintenance costs. Does not provide a long-lasting residual effect unlike other disinfection solutions. Proper safety precautions for operators  are required as ozone is hazardous to handle.

name: Low pressure UV for disinfection
description: LP UV disinfection

name: Inline dosing of ferric chloride
description: Inline dosing of ferric chloride equipment enables in-line mixing. With inline mixing, a concentrated solution of chemicals or additives are dosed directly into a water pipeline.
advantage: Immediate and thorough dispersion of coagulants. Compact design that minimizes the footprint. Reducesthe residence time of the chemical compared to other mixing methods. Lower energy consumption compared to other mixing methods.
disadvantage: May not provide sufficient mixing time or may lead to unven mixing  for the chemicals. Regular maintenance to prevent clogging and fouling. Flow changes may affect mixing efficiency.

name: Dynamic mixer
description: Dynamic mixers enable blending of water with chemicals, e.g. coagulants. In water treatment, dynamic mixers are used to enable mixing coagulation. Mixing coagulation is a water treatment process that combines coagulation and flocculation with dynamic mixing to enhance the removal of suspended particles.
advantage: Provides vigorous agitation, ensuring thorough dispersion of coagulants.Increases the contact between coagulants and suspended particles. Maintains consistent mixing intensity and distribution. Accelerates settling rates.
disadvantage: Energy consumption is fairly high. Proper design and operation of dynamic mixing systems are crucial to avoid issues such as uneven mixing, dead zones, or excessive turbulence. High shear stress in dynamic mixing systems can potentially cause shear damage to flocs, leading to floc breakage.

name: Trickling rapid sand filter
description: Trickling filtration unit with a single filter medium

name: Polymeric ultrafiltration
description: Filtration with membranes that typically removes macromolecules between 1000 and 1000000 Da.

name: UV/H2O2 Advanced Oxidation Process
description: Advanced oxidation with UV and dosing of hydrogen peroxide

name: Chloramine dosing equipment
description: Chloramine is dosed to inactivate micro-organisms and viruses. Chloramines are a group of chemical compounds that contain chlorine and ammonia. Furthermore, chloramine can keep killing germs in water pipes longer than chlorine.
advantage: Chloramination is a highly effective method for killing a wide range of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, and protozoa. Chlorine residuals prevent potential regrowth. Provides rapid action in killing microorganisms.

name: Coagulant dosing with ferric chloride by dynamic mixing
description: Coagulant dosing with ferric chloride using dynamic mixing
advantage: Ferric chloride hydrolyses in water to form iron hydroxide flocs which effectively remove suspended solids, organic matter, and heavy metals from water.

name: Intake pump
description: For the intake, water is transported to the treatment plant via pumps

name: Booster pump
description: If the head of the water intake is not sufficient, additional pumps (booster pumps) are needed.

name: Clean water storage tank
description: Tank to store clean, treated water

name: Coagulant dosing with aluminium chloride by dynamic mixing
description: Coagulant dosing with aluminium chloride
advantage: Adding aluminium chloride to water, which hydrolyze to form positively charged hydroxide complexes that destabilize and aggregate suspended particles, allowing them to be removed by sedimentation or filtration

name: Sludge blanket clarification
description: A sludge blanket clarifier works on the principle of suspended solids capturing other solids as water flows upward through the tank. Instead of solids just settling to the bottom, a suspended “blanket” of sludge forms inside the clarifier and acts as a filter

name: Moving bed sand filtration
description: Moving Bed Rapid Sand Filtration (MBRSF) is a water treatment technology that combines principles of conventional rapid sand filtration with continuous media cleaning. It’s designed to filter out suspended solids, turbidity, and sometimes biological material from raw or partially treated water.

name: Disinfection mixing tank
description: A vessel where a disinfectant agent is dosed and mixed with treated water.

description: Flocculation is a process where flocs are formed after coagulation
